findings.reason: §10's cell can consume the landed `flight.py` derivation now instead of waiting on a parallel `roadmap.py` re-derivation, and the plan should cite flight.py as the existing owner rather than gate itself on work that, for the critical path, is already present.
findings.text: §10 states the critical-path coverage figure "belongs to work-scheduling-surface §3" in `roadmap.py` and holds its cell closed on gate `g-coverage-figure-exists`, but `reckon/flight.py:_path_coverage` (called from `_portfolio_row`, `reckon/flight.py:2080`) already computes exactly that figure — coverage of the critical path's plans from live pointers whose `process_alive` is True rather than from transition events — and it is a plain function callable outside the HTTP handler, already exposed by `reckon flight --portfolio` (`reckon/cli.py:745`) and `crew(view="portfolio")` (`reckon/mcp.py:4481`); commit `d4b581742` asserting it is an ancestor of HEAD and `tests/test_flight_portfolio.py` pins it.

findings.reason: the honest change is to extract the launcher's guard sequence into one callable both the sweep and the dry run use, rather than add a wrapper whose parity rests on a test.
findings.text: `_launcher_refusal()` is a second guard surface that re-checks the launcher's conditions and adds no behaviour `resume_plan()` lacks, and the section text justifies comparing the two surfaces but never says why `resume_plan()` cannot be refactored to expose a guard-only path so both callers share one implementation.

findings.reason: extending `resume_plan()` to expose its guards keeps one source of truth; with a fork a future edit to the launcher's guards leaves the dry run silently wrong.
findings.text: the §6 repair forks `resume_plan()`'s four guards (`launch != "cli"`, live process, budget hold, `resume_window_refusal`) into `reckon/crew/resumption.py:577-620`; the owner of that guard sequence is `resume_plan()` in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, and the fork is held in step only by a parity test, which is the "two implementations of one truth" defect the project's own `AGENTS.md` forbids.

findings.reason: the two helpers are internal to the renderer with no external caller, so the plan need only mark them private (or the section state that nothing is retired), which is a one-line tidy-up rather than a change to what §10 will do.
findings.text: §4 (landed in `4499ca35a`) added the two module-public predicates `declares_a_wait` and `probe_has_run` to `reckon/crew/ticker.py:1435,1453`, contributing to `public_definitions` 1470, and §4's text names nothing it retires or merges and does not state that the two are renderer-local; a `grep` shows no caller outside `ticker.py`, so they are public only by naming convention.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan introduces no new module; every section edits an existing deep module (`recovery.py`'s composer, `ticker.py`'s renderer, `resumption.py`'s sweep) and hides its changes behind those modules' existing interfaces.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §6 fix duplicates the guard sequence owned by `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:resume_plan` into `reckon/crew/resumption.py` rather than extending the owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §4 landed two module-public predicates in `ticker.py` and names nothing it retires or merges, nor states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §10 names only `work-scheduling-surface` §3 / `roadmap.py` as the source of the coverage figure it consumes, and does not cite `reckon/flight.py:_path_coverage`, which already derives that figure.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §6 adds `_launcher_refusal()` as a second, thin guard surface beside the launcher's own guards without saying why `resume_plan()` cannot expose them instead.
